Instance.// Instance: E28-T3. Appear in DataFlow's instance registry. Leave DataFlowBaseUrl or RegistrationSecret empty and this service does not register, which is what a single-instance install wants.

Kestrel.// _comment: E50-T1 host limits, applied by AddHostLimits (Platform.Client/Hosting) — Kestrel does not bind Limits on its own. An env var such as Kestrel__Limits__MaxRequestBodySize overrides one value. A refused request costs nothing past the socket: these are the cheapest limits the server has. Volumetric floods are the reverse proxy's job — see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (Hardening) in the Platform repo.

Limits.// MaxConcurrentConnections: Open connections this process accepts at once; the next one is refused at the socket. null = unlimited (Kestrel's own default).
Limits.// MaxConcurrentUpgradedConnections: WebSocket (upgraded) connections, counted separately because each one lives for minutes or hours.
Limits.// MaxRequestBodySize: Bytes, 30 MB (Kestrel's own default, now stated). A mapping test sends its sample payload in the body.
Limits.// RequestHeadersTimeout: How long a client may take to send its request headers. Short, so a slow-drip client (slowloris) can't hold a connection open for free.

Diagnostics.// LogDirectory: Where the rolling log file goes. Empty = a 'logs' folder beside the binary, which is not writable under Program Files — point a Windows service or a container volume somewhere it can write.
Diagnostics.// MinimumLevel: Verbose | Debug | Information | Warning | Error | Fatal.
Diagnostics.// FailFast: Refuse to start when a preflight check fails, instead of starting and reporting it on /readyz.
